target_customer: Pharma, agriculture, food and chemical companies that outsource organism engineering
problem: Engineering organisms was slow and artisanal, and companies wanted a shared foundry using automation to design custom microbes.
business_model: Fee for service and downstream value share on organism engineering programs, later lab automation products and data

founders.name: Jason Kelly
founders.background_notes: Background not on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Designing organisms at scale needed biology research, DNA assembly automation and software, a research grade problem in 2014.

defensibility.rationale: Foundry scale and accumulated cell programming data were hard to copy, but customers could build in-house teams, which its own filings call the main competitor.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Later filings treat vertically integrated peers as potential customers; Zymergen later failed and Ginkgo acquired it, per mixed sources.

market_need_then: In 2014 the cost of DNA synthesis was falling and companies wanted custom microbes for chemicals, food and pharma; demand shown later by 130 plus customers on the company site.

branding.domain_note: Moved from ginkgobioworks.com to ginkgo.bio, which redirects with a permanent 308

identity.logo: Ginkgo leaf inside a gear, green wordmark, per a design review site
identity.voice_and_tone: Visionary and aspirational, for example 'Someday our kids will design the living world'

branding.brand_signature: Ginkgo leaf in a gear logo and the 'organism company' label
branding.community_and_virality: Wide press as a synbio unicorn and SPAC listing; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Well known in biotech and the 2021 SPAC raised public awareness, but the brand is B2B and no independent brand study was found.

pivots.to: Autonomous labs, cloud lab and data products
pivots.why: Company site now sells lab automation and datapoints; reason not sourced.

outcome_analysis: Ginkgo raised large rounds led by crossover and hedge funds, including a 100 million dollar Series C in 2016, and listed through a SPAC in September 2021. After weak revenue, it cut staff by at least a third in 2024 and its stock fell sharply, so the story is a successful capital raise and listing followed by a hard reset of the business model.
notes: Founder backgrounds are not on the YC page so left empty. Series A and seed amounts conflict across aggregators (9M in 2015-03 or 45M in 2014) and are not recorded. Series B 45M led by Viking Global from one trade article and a TechCrunch mention in search results. Series D 275M dated 2017 or 2019 and a 290M Series E and 70M or 360M in 2020 conflict across aggregators and are unverified; pre-SPAC totals range 785M to 798M. The SPAC date of September 17, 2021 is from Wikipedia only. AgFunder says Senator led the Series C, the press release does not name a lead. The competitor search returned only 2021 to 2026 material so the list is empty. Q1 2024 revenue fell 53 percent and 2024 revenue was 227M including a one-time 45M item per the company release. The YC page says founded 2009, other sources say 2008.
